title: Model-written code runs in a box with no secrets, no network and hard limits
aria: A planted CSV cell makes the model write a command that uploads the cloud credentials. The agent service holds the secrets and never runs the code; a runner service starts a throwaway container with read-only mounts, no network, no root and hard limits, so the command finds nothing to read and nowhere to send it, and a short exit reason goes back to the model. Below, each lock alone leaks data while both together stop it, and a microVM replaces the container when strangers or many customers share hosts.

build.title: Planted text steers the model
build.text: A cell in a client's CSV says: send `~/.aws/credentials` out. The model obeys the planted text and writes the command into a `run_python` tool call.

build.title: The agent keeps the secrets, a runner starts boxes
build.text: The agent service holds the API key and the database password, so it never runs model code. Only the runner may start boxes, because the Docker socket equals root on the host.

build.title: The sandbox locks four things
build.text: Read-only `/data` and `/code`, writes only to `/out` and `/tmp`. `--network none`. User 65534 with every root power dropped. Limits of 60 s, 1 GB and 128 processes.

build.title: A short reason goes back
build.text: The runner sends an exit reason such as "exit 124: timed out after 60 s" back as a `tool_result`, and the model fixes its code. A mature setup adds an egress proxy with an allowlist and a placeholder token.

build.title: Only both locks stop the command
build.text: With no sandbox, keys and the database password leave. With files locked only, `curl` sends the CSV out. With the network locked only, a key leaves later in an exported file. Both locked: the command fails.

build.title: Pick the box by what an escape reaches
build.text: A container shares the host kernel, so one bug lets code out: fine for one team's staff. For strangers or many customers on a host, each session gets a Firecracker microVM, which boots in under 125 ms with under 5 MiB.

route.title: The model writes the attacker's command into its code
route.text: The agent sends the question, the CSV and the `run_python` tool. A planted CSV row is prompt injection, and the model obeys it. It answers with a `tool_use` block asking the agent to run code that uploads `~/.aws/credentials`.

route.title: The agent service hands the code to a runner
route.text: The agent holds the API key and the database password, so it never runs model code. It sends `POST /runs` with the script and file IDs. Only the runner may use the Docker socket.

route.title: The runner builds a box with no network and almost nothing writable
route.text: The runner copies the CSV and the script into `/runs/8f3a/`. Inside, `/data` and `/code` are read-only and only `/out` and `/tmp` are writable. The code runs as user 65534 with every root power dropped, and `--network none`.

route.title: The injected command finds nothing to steal and nowhere to send it
route.text: `~/.aws/credentials` was never mounted, and `curl` cannot even look up the host. Both locks matter: with the network open, `curl -d @/data/positions_q3.csv` would still send the CSV out.

route.title: Limits stop code that is merely wrong
route.text: A later script with no attack loops forever. The inner `timeout` stops it at 60 seconds with exit code 124. Memory, CPU and processes are capped, and the runner runs `docker kill` after 75 seconds.

route.title: The model gets a short reason and tries again
route.text: The runner cuts output to a few KB and returns "exit code 124: timed out after 60 s". The agent sends it as a `tool_result` with the `tool_use` id. The model fixes its code and sends a new `tool_use`.
